name: CurateDistill
description: Training deep neural networks on large-scale datasets incurs substantial computational costs, much of which is spent on redundant or uninformative samples. While knowledge distillation compresses models through teacher–student paradigms, the complementary problem of data-side efficiency remains underexplored. In this paper, we propose CurateDistill, a two-stage framework that combines active data curation with dataset distillation to produce compact yet highly informative training subsets. In the first stage, a pre-trained reference model scores and filters training batches online, prioritizing samples that maximize learning signal while maintaining distributional diversity. In the second stage, distribution-matching distillation compresses the curated subset further via a learnable generator, enabling flexible re-sampling. Experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet show that CurateDistill retains over 92% of the full-dataset accuracy on CIFAR-10/100 and over 82% on the more challenging Tiny-ImageNet, while using only 30% of the data, consistently outperforming random sampling (+8.6%), coreset selection (+5.4%), and standalone dataset distillation (+3.8%) on CIFAR-100 at 30% retention. Student model training cost is reduced by up to 62% when a pre-trained reference model is available; an end-to-end analysis including reference training still yields a 38% cost reduction. The curated–distilled datasets also exhibit cross-architecture generalization across ResNet, VGG, and MobileNet families, suggesting that data-level selection is a practical complement to model-level compression for supervised image classification.
